docs.title: Space Debris SSA Tool
docs.text: A conjunction-screening engine for space situational awareness (SSA). It ingests live two-line element sets (TLEs), propagates orbits with SGP4, finds close approaches to a chosen target object, estimates collision probability, classifies risk, and produces structured reports — exposed through a CLI, a Next.js operator console, and a scheduled GitHub Actions pipeline.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Live TLE ingestion from CelesTrak with a local SQLite cache and staleness tracking.
  • Vectorised SGP4 propagation producing ECI (TEME) state vectors.
  • Target-centric screening: miss distance, refined time of closest approach (TCA), and radial / along-track / cross-track (RAC) geometry.
  • Collision probability (Pc) via Foster's 2D method with Chan's analytic series.
  • Tiered risk classification (critical / watch / nominal).
  • Structured output: canonical CSV + JSON metadata with validation checks.
  • Interactive UI: 3D orbit view, ground tracks, and analytics charts.
  • Automation: scheduled screening with email / webhook alerts.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
pip install -e ".[api,dev]"
sdebris fetch --group iridium-33-debris
sdebris screen --norad 25544 --window-hours 72 --threshold-km 25

Scope & limitations

This is an educational / portfolio tool. TLE-derived Pc is illustrative, not operational — see Methodology. Do not use it for real collision-avoidance decisions.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
CelesTrak GP API
                       │  (TLE text)
                       ▼
   ingest/celestrak.py ── parse ──▶ ingest/cache.py  (SQLite, epoch tracking)
                                          │  SpaceObject[]
                                          ▼
                       propagation/sgp4_prop.py  ── vectorised SGP4 ──▶ Ephemeris
                                          │  (positions/velocities, ECI/TEME)
                                          ▼
   screening/screen.py  ──┬─ coarse distance filter
                          ├─ screening/tca.py     (range-rate bisection → TCA)
                          ├─ screening/frames.py  (RAC decomposition)
                          ├─ risk/pc.py           (Foster + Chan Pc)
                          └─ risk/classify.py     (tiered risk)
                                          │  ScreeningResult (events + metadata)
                          ┌───────────────┼────────────────┐
                          ▼               ▼                ▼
                 reports/writer.py   api/app.py       alerts/notify.py
                 (CSV + JSON)        (FastAPI)        (email / webhook)
                          │               │                │
                          ▼               ▼                ▼
                      CLI (cli.py)   Next.js console  Scheduled CI

docs.title: Modules
docs.text: Package Responsibility config Typed (pydantic) config model + YAML loader with deep merge models SpaceObject, TLE parsing, epoch/age/staleness ingest CelesTrak client + SQLite cache propagation Vectorised SGP4 → Ephemeris (state arrays) screening Target-centric screening, TCA refinement, RAC frames risk Collision probability + tiered classification reports Canonical CSV + JSON metadata with validation alerts Email/webhook dispatch with per-pair cooldown cli sdebris command (Click + Rich)

docs.title: Design choices
docs.text:
• Single config object drives the CLI, the app, and the scheduled job, so every entry point behaves identically.
  • Array-first propagation (Satrec.sgp4_array) keeps screening fast: each object is propagated across the whole time grid in one C call.
  • Coarse-then-refine screening: a cheap per-step distance filter prunes the catalog before the more expensive TCA refinement and Pc computation run only on genuine candidates.
  • Offline resilience: if CelesTrak is unreachable, the pipeline falls back to the cached catalog (or bundled sample TLEs) so demos never hard-fail.

docs.title: Who sees what
docs.text:
The ontology holds three kinds of thing and scopes them differently.

Reference data — space objects, element sets, sensor observations, and the ephemeris derived from them — describes the physical world. There is one ISS. Everyone reads the same rows, and only the ingestion pipeline or an administrator writes them: a bad write here is visible to every reader, which is why those endpoints are admin rather than analyst.

Derived facts — conjunction events and their risk assessments — are computed from that reference data by a deterministic model. Two principals screening the same object get the same answer, so there is nothing in the result to keep private, and the public dashboard is built from exactly these rows.

Work products — screening runs, watch lists, cases, decisions, alerts, manoeuvre scenarios, jobs, commands and the audit trail — record what a particular principal did, and are scoped to them. Note the asymmetry: the run is private while the conjunction it found is public, because screening activity reveals operational interest even when its output does not.

A NULL actor means the platform produced the row — a scheduled screening, a CLI run, the seeded catalogue — and those rows are visible to everyone. That is what lets an anonymous visitor see a real picture rather than an empty one, and it is why the platform keeps its own watch list alongside each principal's.

Administrators read across principals. Everyone else sees their own rows plus the platform's. A request for someone else's row by id returns 404 rather than 403, because confirming that an id exists is itself a disclosure.

sdebris.tenancy is the single place these rules are expressed; call sites pass a column and a principal rather than re-deriving the predicate.

docs.title: Operational layer
docs.text:
The screening engine can persist a completed run into a typed operational ontology. Element sets are append-only and every event is connected to its screening run, input versions, risk assessment, monitoring case, operator decisions, audit actions, and lineage edges.

TLE versions -> ScreeningRun -> ConjunctionEvent -> RiskAssessment
                                      |
                                      v
                                MonitoringCase -> OperatorDecision
                                      |
                                      +-> governed actions + immutable audit

SQLite provides a zero-setup local backend. The SQLAlchemy mappings and Alembic migrations are designed to move to PostgreSQL for deployment. FastAPI exposes the same ontology and action layer to future React/Cesium and agent clients.

docs.title: Serving thousands of readers for nothing
docs.text:
This platform is open source and runs entirely on free tiers. That is a design constraint, not an accident, and two things follow from it that are worth writing down, because both were discovered by measurement rather than guessed at, and both are easy to undo by accident.

The short version: reads are cached so they never reach the API, and sign-in avoids email wherever possible. Everything below is why.

docs.title: What the limits actually were
docs.text:
Measured against the deployed stack, before any of this:

Figure Requests the API answered per second 12.5 Requests one page load sent 23 Page loads per minute, site-wide ~30 Sign-ups possible per hour 2–4

Thirty page loads a minute is not thousands of users. Neither is four sign-ups an hour. They have separate causes and separate fixes.

docs.title: Reads: cached, not recomputed
docs.text:
Nothing an anonymous visitor sees is specific to them. The catalogue, the conjunction list and the trajectories are platform-owned rows, rewritten every six hours by the scheduled screening. Computing them per visitor was pure waste — and expensive waste, because a trajectory runs SGP4 across a time grid and the API has a tenth of a CPU.

Three changes, in increasing order of effect:

  1. Batching. GET /trajectories?norad_ids=… returns every track in one request. The console asked for one per object, which on a twenty-object catalogue was twenty round trips before the first paint finished.
  2. An in-process cache (sdebris/api/public_cache.py) holds the finished JSON for five minutes. A repeat request is a dictionary lookup, not a propagation.
  3. An edge cache (web/app/api/public/[...path]/route.ts). Public reads go to the site's own origin, where a route handler holds the answer and forwards at most one request per interval upstream. This is the one that matters: a response served from the edge never touches the API at all, so it stays fast while the instance is asleep and costs no instance hours.

Anonymous page loads now send one uncached request to the API, down from twenty-three.

docs.title: The rule for adding a route to the cache
docs.text:
The allow-list in the route handler is a security boundary, not an optimisation. That route runs with no bearer token and its answers go into a cache every visitor shares, so a path that reaches it by mistake is both an authorisation bypass and a way to serve one account's rows to the next person.

Only add a path that takes no principal. If the handler's signature mentions PrincipalDep or OptionalPrincipalDep, it does not belong here.

/monitoring is the trap. It looks public, it is readable without signing in, and it returns the platform's watch list to anonymous callers — but a signed-in caller additionally sees their own objects. It is deliberately absent, and web/tests/public-proxy.test.ts fails if it is added.

docs.title: The shared secret
docs.text:
The API meters anonymous traffic by client address. Behind a cache every visitor arrives from the same few addresses, so without an exemption the second person to open the site would be throttled as though they were the first one again.

Set the same value in both places:

  • Render: SDEBRIS_PROXY_TOKEN
  • Vercel: SDEBRIS_PROXY_TOKEN (not NEXT_PUBLIC_, or it ships to the browser and anyone can spend the exemption)

Leave both unset and nothing breaks; the proxy simply gets no exemption, which is the safe default and fine at low traffic.

docs.title: Sign-in: avoid email where possible
docs.text:
Supabase's built-in email sender allows roughly two messages an hour for the whole project. That is a platform limit, not a per-address one, so a visitor who is refused gains nothing by trying another address. At that rate the site cannot accept public sign-ups in any meaningful sense.

Switching from magic links to six-digit codes fixed several real problems — no redirect to misconfigure, no same-browser constraint, no credential in a URL — but it did not touch this one. A code and a link are the same email.

So the platform offers three routes, in this order:

  1. GitHub — first, because the people most likely to want an account on an open-source orbital tool are already reading the repository.
  2. Google — for everyone else.
  3. A six-digit code by email — for people who want neither.

OAuth is unmetered, costs nothing, needs no domain, and never puts a credential in an inbox. Email remains as a genuine fallback, not a token one.

docs.title: Enabling the providers
docs.text:
Both are configured in Supabase → Authentication → Providers, and each needs an OAuth application created with the provider:

Provider Where Callback URL GitHub Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps https://PROJECT.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback Google Google Cloud Console → Credentials → OAuth client ID https://PROJECT.supabase.co/auth/v1/callback

Paste the client ID and secret into Supabase. Until a provider is enabled its button returns "Unsupported provider", which the sign-in page rewrites into something a visitor can act on.

docs.title: Making email work properly
docs.text:
The built-in sender is for development. For real use, configure custom SMTP in Supabase → Project Settings → Authentication → SMTP Settings.

Brevo is the recommendation for this project specifically: 300 emails a day free and permanent, and — unlike most providers — it will verify an individual sender address, so it works without owning a domain. Resend's free tier is larger on paper, but its test domain only delivers to your own address, so real sending needs a domain you have bought.

Two settings, not one. After saving SMTP, raise Authentication → Rate Limits → "Rate limit for sending emails", which has its own conservative default; otherwise one ceiling has been swapped for another.

The email template must contain {{ .Token }}. A template with only {{ .ConfirmationURL }} sends a link, and the code field on the sign-in page will never be satisfied.

docs.title: Keeping the instance awake
docs.text:
.github/workflows/keepwarm.yml pings /ready every ten minutes so Render does not stop the instance after fifteen minutes of quiet, and so Supabase does not pause the project after seven days without a query.

It runs for twelve hours a day rather than twenty-four, and the arithmetic is the reason. The 750 monthly instance-hours belong to the account, not the service, and are shared by every free service on it — this account runs four. Continuous uptime for one costs 744 hours in a 31-day month, leaving nothing for the other three. Running out suspends the service for the rest of the month rather than slowing it down.

Twelve hours (about 370) is defensible rather than stingy because public reads no longer need the instance at all. They are served from the edge, which holds a usable copy through stale-while-revalidate even while the API sleeps. A cold start now delays a signed-in screening run, not the picture a first-time visitor sees. Check the Render dashboard after a week and widen if the hours are there.

Set the repository variable SDEBRIS_API_URL (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables, not Secrets — it is a public URL) or the workflow reports that there is nothing to do and exits.

Two caveats worth knowing:

  • GitHub's scheduler is best-effort and can run twenty minutes late. The job pings three times across each interval so a late start still leaves no gap. A dedicated uptime monitor is more reliable; UptimeRobot's free tier polls every five minutes and takes two minutes to set up.
  • Runner minutes are unmetered on public repositories. On a private one this schedule would exhaust the 2,000-minute monthly allowance in about a week.

docs.title: What breaks next
docs.text:
In the order it will happen, roughly:

  1. Vercel's Hobby plan is non-commercial. Fine for open source, but it conflicts with the paid tier in the billing model. Revenue means Vercel Pro.
  2. Supabase free allows 500 MB of database. Screening results accumulate; old conjunction events are the first thing to prune.
  3. Render's 750 hours, as above, if a second free service appears.
  4. The in-process cache is per-instance. It is correct at one instance and still correct at several, just less effective. The rate limiter is the part that genuinely assumes a single process, and would need Redis before the API is scaled horizontally.

Free-tier figures change often. Verify them against the providers before relying on any number here.

docs.title: Free-tier public deployment
docs.text: This deployment is intended for portfolio demonstration and community feedback, not operational spaceflight decisions. The services below can be configured with no paid resources, subject to each provider's current quotas and acceptable-use policies.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Three services, all on free plans:

  • Vercel Hobby serves the Next.js frontend and managed HTTPS. Both routes prerender as static files, so no serverless functions are involved.
  • Render Free Web Service runs the Docker image containing FastAPI. Screening executes in the API process, so there is no separate worker and no Redis. Render free services sleep after inactivity, so first requests may be slow.
  • Supabase Free provides PostgreSQL and passwordless authentication in one project.

GitHub Actions tests Python, the frontend, browser behavior, migrations, dependencies, and the container on every pull request.

No service key belongs in source control. Copy .env.example locally and enter secrets only in the hosting providers' encrypted environment-variable settings.

docs.title: 1. Supabase
docs.text:
1. Create a free project and enable email magic-link authentication.
  2. Add the Vercel production URL and preview URLs to Auth redirect URLs.
  3. Confirm the project signs tokens asymmetrically. Under Authentication -> JWT Keys, the active key must be ES256 or RS256. The API verifies tokens through the JWKS endpoint and accepts only those two algorithms, so a project still on the legacy shared HS256 secret publishes an empty key set and every signed-in request fails with 401. Migrating to a signing key is done from that page and needs no code change.
  4. Copy the transaction-pooler connection string. Change its scheme to postgresql+psycopg:// and store it as SDEBRIS_DATABASE_URL on Render. The pooler runs on port 6543 and is reachable over IPv4; the direct connection on 5432 is IPv6-only on the free tier and will not resolve from many networks.
  5. Set these Render variables using the project URL:
SDEBRIS_AUTH_JWKS_URL=https://PROJECT.supabase.co/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json
SDEBRIS_AUTH_ISSUER=https://PROJECT.supabase.co/auth/v1
SDEBRIS_AUTH_AUDIENCE=authenticated

docs.title: Pushing the schema
docs.text:
Render applies migrations on every deploy, so a deployed stack needs nothing further. To build the schema by hand — before the first deploy, or to run a local API against the hosted database — put the pooler URL in .env at the repository root and run:

alembic upgrade head

.env is read by the API, the CLI and Alembic alike, and never overrides a variable already set in the real environment.

docs.title: Why the tables are closed to PostgREST
docs.text:
Supabase publishes every table in the public schema through PostgREST, and the anon key that authorises those requests is compiled into the browser bundle. This platform never reads its data that way: the frontend holds a Supabase JWT only in order to call the API, which connects to Postgres as the owning role and applies its own role and quota checks.

That leaves PostgREST as pure attack surface. Without intervention, anyone with the public anon key could read entitlements straight out of the database — customer emails and plan status — and write to it. Migration 8f2d4e1a6b07_restrict_postgrest_exposure closes it with two independent locks: privileges are revoked from anon and authenticated, including the default privileges that would otherwise be inherited by tables added later, and row level security is enabled on every table with no policy attached. An empty policy set denies every row to every non-owning role, so a privilege granted back by mistake still yields nothing.

There are deliberately no per-user policies. Nothing ever connects as an end user, so a policy written against auth.uid() would gate a code path that does not exist, while reading as though the data were protected by it.

Confirm the lock after migrating, from the SQL editor:

set role anon;
select * from entitlements;   -- expected: permission denied for table entitlements
reset role;
select tablename from pg_tables
where schemaname = 'public' and not rowsecurity;   -- expected: no rows

Supabase is not optional in production. The API refuses to start without SDEBRIS_AUTH_JWKS_URL when SDEBRIS_ENV=production, and the local development-token endpoint returns 404 outside development, so a deployment without a JWKS issuer has no way for anyone to sign in.

docs.title: Roles are assigned automatically
docs.text:
Roles are not set by hand. Migration b7e3c05d19af installs a Supabase custom access token hook, public.custom_access_token_hook, which stamps app_metadata.role into every JWT as it is minted. The mapping lives in the role_grants table, keyed by email: an exact match wins, and the * row supplies the default for everyone else.

Enable it once, in the dashboard: Authentication -> Hooks -> Customize Access Token (JWT) Claims, selecting custom_access_token_hook. Until that is done the function exists but nothing calls it, and every account falls back to viewer — the API treats a missing or unrecognised role as viewer, so an unconfigured hook fails safe rather than open.

Granting someone operator, which is a job function rather than something bought, is one row:

insert into role_grants (email, role, note)
values ('person@example.com', 'operator', 'Runs case workflow');

Raising the default once the ontology is per-tenant is one update:

update role_grants set role = 'analyst' where email = '*';

Neither needs a migration or a redeploy; both take effect at the person's next sign-in, because a JWT keeps whatever claims it was issued with until it expires. The same applies to a revocation — plan changes are read live from the database on every request, but a role change requires a new token, which is one reason billing is deliberately not expressed as a role.

The hook overwrites app_metadata.role rather than merging it, so a value a client managed to get into its own metadata cannot survive into a verified token.

docs.title: What an anonymous visitor can see
docs.text:
The public picture is deliberately real: the tracked catalogue, element sets, propagated trajectories, conjunction events and their plain-language explanations are all readable without an account, so the dashboard means something before anyone signs up. Operational state is not: monitoring cases, the activity feed, billing and every write require a token.

Anonymous traffic is metered by client address instead of by principal, since there is no identity to meter. Reads get a generous per-minute budget; trajectory propagation, which runs SGP4 over a grid of up to 8640 points, gets a much tighter one. Behind a proxy the address is taken from the rightmost X-Forwarded-For hop, which the caller cannot forge.

docs.title: 2. Render API
docs.text:
Create a Blueprint from render.yaml. Enter every variable marked sync: false. Set:

SDEBRIS_CORS_ORIGINS=https://YOUR_VERCEL_DOMAIN

Vercel gives each preview deployment its own hostname, which cannot be listed in advance. To let previews reach the API, also set a pattern that matches only your own preview domains:

SDEBRIS_CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX=https://YOUR_PROJECT-[a-z0-9-]+\.vercel\.app

Leave it unset to refuse previews. The pattern is matched against the whole origin, so it cannot be widened accidentally by a suffix such as https://YOUR_PROJECT.attacker.example. An invalid pattern fails at startup rather than silently blocking every request.

The container applies migrations and then binds FastAPI to Render's $PORT. /health is a process liveness check; /ready also verifies database connectivity. Render terminates public TLS.

Free Render services sleep after inactivity and provide an ephemeral filesystem. All durable application state therefore belongs in Supabase. Cached TLE files may disappear safely and will be refreshed.

docs.title: Job execution on the free plan
docs.text:
render.yaml sets SDEBRIS_JOB_BACKEND=thread. Screening runs on a thread pool inside the API process, which suits a single free instance and removes the need for a Redis broker. The trade-off is durability: a job in flight is lost if the instance restarts or sleeps. Screening runs are short, so in practice this means re-running the command.

For a durable queue, set SDEBRIS_JOB_BACKEND=redis and supply SDEBRIS_REDIS_URL (Upstash offers a free Redis database). The container then also starts one Dramatiq worker. With the thread backend it starts no worker at all.

docs.title: 3. Vercel frontend
docs.text:
Import the repository, set the root directory to web, and configure:

NEXT_PUBLIC_SDEBRIS_API_URL=https://YOUR_API.onrender.com
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://PROJECT.supabase.co
NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=YOUR_PUBLISHABLE_ANON_KEY
SDEBRIS_PROXY_TOKEN=SHARED_WITH_RENDER

SDEBRIS_PROXY_TOKEN is deliberately not a NEXT_PUBLIC_ value: it is read by the caching route handler on the server, and shipping it to the browser would let anyone spend the rate-limit exemption it buys. Set the same value on Render. See capacity.md.

NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are inlined at build time, so changing one requires a redeploy rather than only an environment-variable edit.

The build script copies Cesium's runtime assets into public/cesium (about 23 MB, git-ignored and regenerated on every build), so no extra configuration is needed for the globe.

The Supabase anon/publishable key is designed for browser use. The service-role key is privileged and must never be added to Vercel or exposed as NEXT_PUBLIC_*.

docs.title: 4. Billing (Dodo Payments)
docs.text:
Dodo Payments is a merchant of record: it is the legal seller, collects in USD worldwide, handles VAT/GST/sales tax, and remits to an Indian bank account. That is what makes it workable where Stripe is not.

Create a product for the Pro plan, then point its webhook at:

https://YOUR_API.onrender.com/billing/webhook

Copy the signing secret into Render as SDEBRIS_BILLING_WEBHOOK_SECRET. Until that variable is set the endpoint returns 503 for every delivery — it never falls back to trusting unsigned input.

Deliveries are verified against the Standard Webhooks scheme: webhook-id, webhook-timestamp and webhook-signature headers over an HMAC-SHA256 of {id}.{timestamp}.{body}, with a five-minute replay window. Check the header and event names against Dodo's current documentation before going live — the signature algorithm is a published standard and stable, but event naming is the part most likely to have changed. The names this build recognises are in GRANTING_EVENTS and REVOKING_EVENTS in src/sdebris/billing/webhooks.py; adding one is a dictionary entry.

Grants are keyed on the buyer's email, because that is all a merchant of record knows at checkout. The auth subject is attached on their first signed-in request, so buying and signing up can happen in either order. Every delivery is recorded in billing_events and is idempotent on the provider's event id, so a retry renews a grant rather than stacking a second one.

To comp an account without a payment, insert a row in entitlements with plan='pro', status='active', the person's email, and a null expires_at for lifetime access.

docs.title: 5. Backups
docs.text:
Supabase Free does not provide point-in-time recovery. Run a logical backup before migrations and periodically from a trusted computer with pg_dump:

.\scripts\backup_database.ps1 -DatabaseUrl $env:SDEBRIS_DATABASE_URL

Backup files are ignored by Git. Store encrypted copies in a private location. Test recovery periodically with pg_restore into a disposable database.

docs.title: 6. Public-launch checklist
docs.text:
• Confirm /health, /ready, and /methodology return successfully.
  • Confirm an anonymous mutation returns 401.
  • Confirm a viewer cannot start screening and receives 403.
  • Confirm an analyst can enqueue a screening and receives progress events.
  • Confirm /billing/webhook returns 400 for an unsigned delivery.
  • Confirm a free account is refused a window over 24 hours with 402.
  • Confirm the live activity stream connects: the console header should read STREAM LIVE rather than STREAM OFFLINE.
  • Restrict Supabase redirects and API CORS to the deployed domains.
  • Enable repository branch protection and required CI checks.
  • Add issue templates for bug reports and scientific-method feedback.
  • Put the non-operational limitation in the repository description and launch post.
  • Enable the GitHub and Google providers in Supabase, and check each button completes a round trip rather than returning "Unsupported provider".
  • Configure custom SMTP and raise the email rate limit. Until this is done the project can send about two messages an hour and public sign-up by email does not work; OAuth is unaffected.
  • Confirm the email template contains {{ .Token }}, or no code is sent.
  • Set SDEBRIS_PROXY_TOKEN to the same value on Render and Vercel.
  • Set the SDEBRIS_API_URL repository variable so the keep-warm workflow runs.
  • Confirm /api/public/monitoring returns 404 and /api/public/events/assessed returns 200: the first is the cache's authorisation boundary.

docs.title: Free-tier limitations
docs.text:
This stack may cold-start, pause after inactivity, and enforce storage, bandwidth, or build quotas. It is public-deployment-ready for a low-traffic portfolio, not high availability. Configure spend caps or omit billing details where providers allow it; exceeding a free quota should suspend service rather than incur charges.

Three consequences are specific to this application:

  • Cold starts are visible. After the Render service sleeps, the first request can take roughly a minute. The console degrades honestly rather than breaking: the activity feed reconnects with exponential backoff and its header reports RECONNECTING, then OFFLINE after repeated failures, while continuing to retry.
  • Instance hours are the binding constraint, not traffic. The console holds a Server-Sent Events connection open for the activity feed, so the instance does not idle while anyone has the page open, and the keep-warm workflow pings it deliberately for eighteen hours a day. Both spend from the same 750-hour monthly allowance, which is shared across every free service on the account. Public reads no longer contribute, because they are served from the edge without reaching the instance at all.
  • Supabase free projects pause after a period of inactivity and need to be resumed from the dashboard, which matters for a portfolio link that is visited irregularly.

If the cold starts and pauses become a problem, the component to move first is the API: an always-on host (for example an Oracle Cloud Always Free VM) removes both, and the frontend and database can stay where they are.

docs.title: Scientific methodology
docs.text: This page documents the models behind the numbers and, importantly, their limitations.

docs.title: 1. Orbit propagation (SGP4)
docs.text:
TLEs are propagated with the standard SGP4 model (via the sgp4 library), producing position and velocity in the TEME (True Equator, Mean Equinox) ECI frame. SGP4 is the analytic model TLEs are fitted to, so it is the correct propagator for this data source.

Accuracy. SGP4/TLE position error is typically on the order of ~1 km near epoch and grows to several km over days. This is fundamental to the data source and bounds everything downstream.

docs.title: 2. Close-approach screening
docs.text: For a chosen target, every catalog object is propagated over the same time grid. A cheap per-step Euclidean distance gives a coarse minimum; objects whose coarse minimum exceeds coarse_threshold_km are discarded.

docs.title: 3. Time of Closest Approach (TCA)
docs.text:
The coarse grid brackets but rarely lands on the true minimum. At the true TCA the range-rate vanishes:

$$ g(t) = \mathbf{dr}(t)\cdot \mathbf{dv}(t) = 0 $$

where $\mathbf{dr}$ and $\mathbf{dv}$ are the relative position and velocity. We locate the coarse minimum, then bisect $g$ over the neighbouring interval, interpolating both state vectors to the root. This refines the miss distance and the relative velocity at closest approach.

docs.title: 4. RAC (RIC) decomposition
docs.text:
The relative position at TCA is projected into the target's RIC frame:

$$ \hat{R} = \frac{\mathbf{r}}{|\mathbf{r}|}, \quad \hat{C} = \frac{\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{v}}{|\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{v}|}, \quad \hat{I} = \hat{C}\times\hat{R} $$

giving the radial, along-track, and cross-track miss components. Conjunction geometry is usually along-track dominated.

docs.title: 5. Collision probability (Pc)
docs.text:
We use Foster's 2D method:

  1. Build the conjunction plane perpendicular to the relative velocity at TCA.
  2. Project the combined position covariance and the miss vector into that plane.
  3. Rotate to the covariance's principal axes ($\sigma_x, \sigma_y$) and evaluate Chan's series for a circular hard-body cross-section of radius $R$:

$$ P_c = e^{-v/2}\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\frac{v^m}{2^m m!} \left[1 - e^{-u/2}\sum_{k=0}^{m}\frac{u^k}{2^k k!}\right], \quad u=\frac{R^2}{\sigma_x\sigma_y},\; v=\frac{x_m^2}{\sigma_x^2}+\frac{y_m^2}{\sigma_y^2} $$

docs.title: Where the covariance comes from — and the big caveat
docs.text:
TLEs carry no covariance

Operational Pc uses covariance supplied by the owner/operator or the 18th Space Defense Squadron. TLEs do not include uncertainty. This tool therefore synthesises a covariance as a documented surrogate:

  • A diagonal RIC 1-σ uncertainty (radial / along-track / cross-track), with along-track the largest — matching how SGP4 error actually behaves.
  • The 1-σ values grow linearly with TLE age (age_growth_m_per_day), encoding the intuition that stale elements are less trustworthy.

Consequently the Pc values here are illustrative, not operational. They are useful for relative ranking and for demonstrating the method — not for real conjunction-avoidance decisions.

docs.title: 6. Risk classification
docs.text:
Each event takes the highest tier whose miss-distance OR Pc condition is met:

Tier Default trigger critical miss ≤ 1 km or Pc ≥ 1e-4 watch miss ≤ 5 km or Pc ≥ 1e-5 nominal everything else

Thresholds are fully configurable in configs/default.yaml.

docs.title: Summary of limitations
docs.text:
• TLE/SGP4 position accuracy (~km, degrading with age).
  • Synthetic (age-based) covariance, not real operator covariance.
  • 2D analytic Pc assumes Gaussian, linear relative motion through the encounter.
  • No atmospheric-drag re-fitting, maneuver detection, or sensor tasking.

docs.title: Operational ontology
docs.text: The ontology service turns screening output into connected, versioned operational objects. It is intentionally separate from the screening pipeline that feeds it.

docs.title: Object model
docs.text:
Object Purpose SpaceObject Canonical identity for a NORAD catalog object ElementSet Append-only orbital element version Ephemeris Propagated state associated with a run and element version ConjunctionEvent Close approach between two objects RiskAssessment Versioned risk interpretation for an event MonitoringCase Owned operational workflow opened from an event SensorObservation Source-attributed measured state ManeuverScenario Simulation of a possible mitigation Alert Delivery and acknowledgement state OperatorDecision Human decision, justification, and approval

AuditAction records before/after state, actor, justification, approvals, and data/model versions for governed actions. LineageEdge connects source and derived objects without replacing the typed domain schema with an EAV model.

docs.title: Local startup
docs.text:
Install the API dependencies and initialize the local SQLite database:

pip install -e ".[api,dev]"
sdebris ontology-init
Run the API:

sdebris-api

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs for the generated OpenAPI interface.

To persist a screening run and automatically open cases for critical events:

sdebris screen --norad 25544 --persist-ontology

docs.title: Database configuration
docs.text:
The zero-configuration backend is sqlite:///data/ontology.sqlite. Deployments should set:

SDEBRIS_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://user:password@host/database

Run managed schema upgrades with:

alembic upgrade head

The initial migration defines all ontology, lineage, and audit tables. PostgreSQL requires a compatible driver such as psycopg.

docs.title: Governed actions
docs.text:
The API currently supports:

  • open, assign, escalate, and close a monitoring case;
  • request an orbit refresh or screening rerun;
  • acknowledge an alert;
  • record an operator decision;
  • create a maneuver scenario;
  • capture notification requests.

Action requests are immutable audit events. Worker-only requests such as orbit refresh and notification are recorded now and are intended for consumption by a durable workflow engine in the next platform milestone.

docs.title: API outline
docs.text:
GET    /ontology
POST   /objects
POST   /objects/{norad}/element-sets
POST   /objects/{norad}/observations
POST   /screening-runs
POST   /events
POST   /events/{id}/assessments
POST   /events/{id}/cases
POST   /events/{id}/maneuvers
POST   /cases/{id}/actions/{action}
POST   /cases/{id}/decisions
POST   /alerts/{id}/acknowledge
GET    /events/assessed
GET    /activity
GET    /stream/activity
GET    /audit-actions
GET    /lineage/{entity_type}/{entity_id}

GET /activity returns one chronological feed merging conjunctions, alerts, screening-job transitions, command executions, monitoring changes, and audited governance actions. GET /stream/activity serves the same items as Server-Sent Events. Both are cursor-based: every item carries an occurred_at timestamp and a client resumes from the last one it saw, so a dropped connection replays what was missed without duplicating what was already delivered.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
git clone <repo-url>
cd "Space debris SSA tool"
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate   # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -e ".[app,dev,docs]"

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The package installs a sdebris command.

# Refresh the local TLE cache from CelesTrak
sdebris fetch --group iridium-33-debris

# Inspect the cache
sdebris catalog

# Screen the catalog against a target (ISS = 25544)
sdebris screen --norad 25544 --window-hours 72 --threshold-km 25

# Offline (cache only) + dispatch alerts for critical events
sdebris screen --norad 25544 --no-fetch --alert

docs.title: Key screen options
docs.text: Option Meaning --norad Target NORAD catalog id (required) --group CelesTrak group to screen against --window-hours Look-ahead propagation window --step-sec Coarse propagation step --threshold-km Report only approaches closer than this --start ISO-8601 UTC start time (default: now) --no-fetch Use the cache only; skip CelesTrak --alert Send email / webhook alerts for critical events --config Path to a YAML config overriding the defaults

docs.title: Operator console
docs.text:
The web interface is the Next.js app in web/, backed by the FastAPI service. Run both:

sdebris-api                       # FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8000
cd web && npm install && npm run dev   # console on localhost:3000

Everything is driven from one typed command surface, parsed against an allowlist. The console shows the orbital picture in 3D, a live activity stream, telemetry for the selected object, and streaming progress for screening jobs. Open /docs in the app for the full command reference, or press the TOUR button for a guided walkthrough.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All behaviour is driven by configs/default.yaml. Copy it, edit, and pass with --config my.yaml, or override individual fields via CLI flags. See the file's inline comments for every option (thresholds, uncertainty model, alerts, etc.).

docs.title: Alerts
docs.text:
Set delivery channels in config (alerts.email, alerts.webhook) and provide secrets via environment variables:

export SDEBRIS_WEBHOOK_URL="https://hooks.slack.com/services/..."
export SDEBRIS_SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com
export SDEBRIS_SMTP_USER=...  SDEBRIS_SMTP_PASSWORD=...

A per-pair cooldown (alerts.cooldown_hours) suppresses repeat alerts.
